resources.title: Importance and Forms of Agriculture
resources.description: Theme: CONCEPT AND MEDIUM OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Sub-theme: CONCEPT AND MEDIUM OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Content: 1. Importance of agriculture in the society: - source of food - clothing etc. 2. Type of agricultural practices in the localities: - pastoral farming - arable farming etc. 3. Forms of agricultural activities in the communities: - growing crops - rearing livestock - rearing of fish - salving of farm produce etc.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. state the importance of agriculture 2. explain the type of agriculture. 3. state Forms agricultural practices.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides class discussion on the importance of agriculture through agriculture. 2. Guide class discussion on the type of agricultural practices. 3. Guides class to discuss on forms of Agricultural activities. 4. Give a board summary.

Students: 1. Guide discussion on agricultural importance in their local communities 2. Guided discussion on agriculture. 3. Copy the board summary
resources.resources: 1. Posters showing the importance of agriculture. 2. Pamphlets, handbills and charts showing type of agriculture. 3. Charts and pictures of various forms of agricultural activities. 4. Specimen of farm produce e.g. Yam, Orange, etc.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. explain the importance of agriculture; 2. identify the different types of agricultural practices; 3. name three forms of agricultural activities in their locality.

resources.title: Classes and Uses of Crops.
resources.description: Theme: CONCEPT AND MEDIUM OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Sub-theme: CONCEPT AND MEDIUM OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Content: 1. Crop Plant Forms: - Monocotyledonous e.g. maize, guinea corn. - Dicotyledonous e.g. bean, melon. 2. Classification of Crops based on: - Life span:- annuals (e.g. maize, yam), etc. - Perennials (e.g. cocoa, mango), etc. 3. Uses of Crops: - food e.g. cereals, tubers, pulses, fruits and vegetables - oil crops - spices - latex - beverage - fiber crops - source of carbohydrate, protein, fat and oil, minerals, vitamin etc.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. identify crop plant forms; 2. classify crops according to forms, life span, uses, and types; 3. state the various uses of crops.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1 Guides discussion on various plant forms. 2. Displays samples of crops from each of the classes for students to see. 3. Provides students with different types of crops and ask them to classify based on forms, life span, uses and types. 4. Give a board summary

Students: 1. Sorts crops into various classes. 2. Classify crops according to: - forms, - life, - span, - types, and uses. 3. Copy the board summary
resources.resources: 1. Specimen of monocotyledon ous and dicotyledonous seeds. 2. Crop sample pictures and charts depicting the various classes of crops
resources.assessment: Students to: 1 List two crop plant forms; 2 Sort and classify the specimen provided into the plant forms; 3 List two external features of crop plant forms; 4. classify the displayed crops based on the life span; 5. match the crop samples with their respective uses; 6. Students to classify the following crops: Maize, beans, waterleaf, soya- beans, cassava, pepper, cocoa etc. according to their forms, uses and life span.

resources.title: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals
resources.description: Theme: CONCEPT AND MEDIUM OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Sub-theme: CONCEPT AND MEDIUM OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Content: 1. Types of Farm Animals: - Work animals - Diary animals - Guard animals - Poultry - Aquatic animals - Pets, etc. 2. Basic characteristics of farm animals. 3. Classification of farm animals based on: i. Size - Large animals - Small animals ii. Habitat: - Aquatic - Terrestrial Iii Mammals & non- mammals iv. Stomach types: - Ruminant and - Non ruminant animals 4. Uses of farm animals: - Food - Work - Sports and guard - Source of hides and skin - Source of manure.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. describe different forms of farm animals; 2. identify the basic characteristics of different farm animals; 3. list farm animals found in their locality; 4. classify farm animals based on: - size - habitat 5. state the uses of farm animals.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides students in observing and identifying farm animals. 2. Displays charts showing external features of some farm animals. 3. Explains the various uses of farm animals. 4. Give a board summary

Students: 1. Observe and identify various forms of farm animals based on their distinct features. 2. Familiarise self with various types of farm animals by studying the charts and pictures. 3. Discuss the uses of farm animals. 4. Copy the board summary.
resources.resources: 1. Pictures/charts of various specimen of the farm animal forms like bull, goat, dog, turkey, fish, etc. 2. Charts and picture of various farm animals
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. state the features of the different forms of farm animals. 2. list five farm animals. 3. match farm animals with their uses.

resources.title: Methods of Weed and Pests Control.
resources.description: Theme: CONCEPT AND MEDIUM OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Sub-theme: CONCEPT AND MEDIUM OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Content: 1. Characteristics of Weeds: - Easily Dispersed - Long Dormancy, 3. Uses of weeds - Medicinal. - Food, etc. 3. Methods of weed control - Rotation of crop - Herbicides, etc. 4. Effects of weed control methods on vegetation and soil: - pollution of soil and ground water - contamination of livestock pasture, etc. 5. Classification of insect pests based on mouth parts - piercing and sucking insects - biting and chewing insects 6. Description of the damage done by the crop pests. 7. Effects of crop pests on yield.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. list the characteristics of weeds. 2. indicate the uses of weeds. 3. briefly discuss methods of weed control. 4. state the effects of weed control methods on vegetation and soil. 5. classify insect pests according to mouth parts. 6. describe the nature of damage done by crop plant pests. 7. state effects of pests on the crop yield.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Demonstrates chemical control of weeds 2. Highlights the effects of weeds control methods on vegetation and soil 3. Displays pictures and charts of crop pests of the locality. 4. Displays specimen of insect pests. 4. Give a board summary

Students: 1. Practice weed control on the school farm. 2. Study pictures and charts to familiarize self with the local crop plant pest. 3. Bring insect pests and make insect box. 5. Copy the board summary.
resources.resources: 1. Charts and pictures of weeds. 2. Weeds specimens. 3. Weed album. 4. Herbicides. 5. Charts and pictures of the pests of the locality 6. Specimens of insect pest, formalin, kerosene, (for preservation), insect box, etc.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. mention two characteristics of weeds. 2. state two uses of weeds. 3. state two weed control methods. 4. explain two effects of weed control on the environment. 5. mention two classes of crop pests 6. list two piercing and sucking insect and three biting and chewing insects. 7. describe the nature of damage done by crop plant pests.

resources.title: Factors of Agricultural Production
resources.description: Theme: CONCEPT AND MEDIUM OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Sub-theme: CONCEPT AND MEDIUM OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Content: Factors of Production: - land - labour - water - money - management
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. list the basic factors of production. 2. describe the uses of each in Agricultural production.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. States the factors of production. 2. Discusses the importance of each factor in production.

Students: Pick one factor of production and Write a short essay on it.
resources.resources: Flow chart of production processes.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. mention three basic factors of production. 2. state the importance of each factor in production.

resources.title: Puberty, Adolescence, Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs), HIV/AIDS and Human Rights
resources.description: Theme: FAMILY LIVING AND RESOURCE MANAGEMENT | Sub-theme: FAMILY LIVING AND RESOURCE MANAGEMENT | Content: 1. Meaning of puberty and adolescence; 2. Signs of puberty; 3. Needs and challenges of the adolescent; 4. Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) and HIV/AIDS; 5. Fundamental human rights and rights of the child.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of puberty and adolescence; 2. describe the signs of puberty in boys and girls; 3. discuss the needs and challenges of the adolescent; 4. explain the meaning, causes, signs and prevention of sexually transmitted infection (STIs) and HIV/AIDS; 5. enumerate the rights of the child
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the meanings of puberty, adolescence, STIs and HIV/AIDS, human rights; 2. Leads students on discussion on the issues explained 3. Gives a board summary.

Students: 1. Participate actively in discussion 2. Copy the board summary
resources.resources: Charts and pictures on puberty, adolescence and people infected with STIs and HIV/AIDS
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. explain the meaning of puberty; 2. explain the meaning of adolescence; 3. state three each, of the signs of puberty in boys and girls; 4. state three hygiene guides for an adolescent 5. state three causes of STIs 6. list three rights of a child.

resources.title: Family Needs, Goals and Standards
resources.description: Theme: FAMILY LIVING AND RESOURCE MANAGEMENT | Sub-theme: FAMILY LIVING AND RESOURCE MANAGEMENT | Content: 1. Meaning and types of family needs and wants; 2. Meaning of family goals and standards. 3. Relationship among family needs, goals and standards; 4. Uses of family needs, goals and standard in resource management. .
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of family needs; 2. list family needs e.g. food, clothing, shelter, etc 3. explain the meaning of family goals and standards; 4. discuss the relationship among the family needs, goals and standards; 5. explain family resource management; 6. state the ways family needs,goals and standard help in family resource management.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the meaning of family needs, goals and standards; 2. Leads class in discussion; 3. Gives students assignment; 4. Gives a board summary.

Students: 1. Participate in the discussion; 2. Give examples of individual goals and standards; 3. Copy the board summary.
resources.resources: Charts on family needs, goals and standards.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. explain the meaning of family need, goal and standard; 2. state two examples of family needs; 3. differentiate among family needs goal and satandard; 4. enumerate any five familiy goals; 5. explain the meaning of family standard. 6. state the ways family needs, goals and standard help in family resource management.

resources.title: Production of Clothing and Household Articles/Crafts
resources.description: Theme: CLOTHING AND TEXTILE | Sub-theme: CLOTHING AND TEXTILE | Content: 1. List and explain simple relevant household articles and crafts; 2. Tool, equipment and materials for making simple articles and crafts; 3. Construction of simple relevant articles e.g. apron, cap, needlework bag, head rest, table mat, puffs, purse, curtain holder, bibs, armrest, shopping bag, napkins and handkerchief, head- tie. 4. Production of income yielding crafts e.g. tie/dye and batik fabrics
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. list household articles 2. discuss how to produce simple articles like apron, cap, tray cloth, needle- work bag, handkerchief. 3. list tools, equipment and materials for making simple household articles and craft items; 4. make simple household articles and crafts for sale.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Lists the simple household articles and craft 2. Discusses the materials, tools equipment for making simple household articles and crafts. 3. Demonstrates how to make any of the chosen items; improvise where neccesary 4. Demonstrates how to make some income yielding articles. Improvise where necessary 5. Displays/ exhibits products for sale. 6. Gives a board summary

Students: 1. List house hold articles. 2. Mention the materials and tools for making simple household articles and crafts. 3. Practice the making of a household article and a simple craft. 4. Display/exhibit produced articles. 5. Copy the board summary.
resources.resources: 1. Finished apron, cap, tray cloth and needle work bag, handkerchief , some ready made crafts. 2. Materials tools and equipment for making crafts 3. Pieces of calico/baft cloth, thread, needle, sewing kit.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. list the articles and tools, steps involved in making simple household articles and household article and craft. 2. list the items needed to construct a tray cloth; 3. list the tools for making any two crafts, 4. make and display the articles and crafts constructed.

resources.title: Production of Cleaning Agents, Deodorants and Cosmetics
resources.description: Theme: HOME MANAGEMENT | Sub-theme: HOME MANAGEMENT | Content: 1. Types of home- made cleaning agents. 2. Uses of home- made cleaning agents. 3. Preparation of home- made cleaning agents. 4. Using home-made polish and cleaning agents. 5. Types of cosmetics 6. Materials and tools for making cosmetics e.g. pomade, cream and deodorants. 7. Safety, quality and regulatory control of cosmetic products in Nigeria. 8. Role of regulatory bodies e.g. NAFDAC, SON, etc. 9. Procedure for making cream/pomade, deodorants and cosmetics.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. identify different types of home-made cleaning agents; 2. state the uses of different home-made cleaning agents; 3. prepare home- made polish and different cleaning agents; 4. discuss safety, quality and regulatory control of cosmetic products 5. list materials and tools for making cosmetics e.g. pomade/cream; 6. make cosmetics e.g. pomade, cream, and cosmetics.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Discusses types of home-made polish and cleaning agents 2. Explains steps in the production of home- made polish and cleaning agents. 3. Demonstrates making of home-made furniture polish and cleaning agents. 4. Prepares different samples of home-made furniture polish and cleaning agents and display in class. 5. Lists materials and tools for making pomade, cream, etc. 6. Explains steps in making pomade and cream 7. Displays actual products, materials and tools for making pomade/cream and deodorant 8. Discusses the safety, quality and regulatory control of cosmetic products 9. Gives a board summary.

Students: 1. Examine samples of home-made furniture polish and cleaning agents, pomade/cream, anddeodorants displayed. 2. List and discuss the steps in the production of home-made polish. 3. Practice the production polish. 4. Practice the making of cleaning agents, pomade/cream and deodrant. 5. Display the products made. 6. Copy the board summary
resources.resources: 1. Kerosene/turpenti ne, candle wax, bar soap and palm oil; 2. Pawpaw and pineapple leaves, fine sand, detergent, grater, sauce pan, ground egg shell, wood ash, lime, salt and water 3. Wooden furniture e.g. table, chairs, cupboards, shelves etc 4. Galvanized iron e.g. saucepan, pots, buckets, cutlery, water. 5. Charts showing different stages in preparing home- made polish and cleaning agents, cream/pomade and deodorants 6. Real objects of prepared cleaning agents, cream and cosmetics.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. list different types of home made cleaning agent 2. list of steps involved in the production of home-made furniture polish; 3. give two examples of home-made cleaning agents; 4. make and display furniture polish and other cleaning agents 5. polish some furniture in the classroom; 6. discuss importance of safety and regulatory control of cosmetic products 7. make and display pomade/cream, and deodorants.

resources.title: Healthy Feeding and Eating Practices
resources.description: Theme: FOOD AND NUTRITION | Sub-theme: FOOD AND NUTRITION | Content: 1. Healthy feeding practices include e.g. - eat adequate diet, - use foods in season. 2. Healthy eating habits e.g. - washing hands before and after eating; - taking a small quantity of food at a time; - chewing food properly; - talking (if you have to) without food in the mouth. 3. Effect of unhealthy feeding practices e.g. marasmus, kwashiorkor, obesity, etc 4. Effects of unhealthy eating habits e.g. - Stomach ache 5. Food additives: uses, misuses and detection 6. Food contaminants 7. Harmful substances that should not be consumed e.g. banned additives, spoilt fruits, under-cooked food, etc. 8. Meaning of drug abuse. 9. Effects of drug abuse in the body.
resources.objectives: The students should be able to: 1. mention healthy feeding and eating practices; 2. state the effects of healthy feeding practices; 3. state the effects of healthy eating habits 4. identify food additives and harmful substances that should not be taken into the body; 5. state the effects of harmful substances in the body. 6. define drug abuse and effects on human beings.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Discusses healthy feeding and eating practices 2. Demonstrates good feeding and eating practices 3. Discusses the effects of unhealthy feeding and eating practices 4. Explains food additives and contaminants 5. Discusses harmful substances that should not be taken into the body 6. Discusses effects of drug abuse. 7. Displays diagrams of harmful substances. 8. Gives a board summary.

Students: 1. Participates in the class discussion 2. Discuss effects of: - talking while eating; - eating too much; - drinking water while eating 3. Dramatize the effects of harmful substances to the body. 4. Display and identify diagrams of harmful substances 5. Copy the board summary.
resources.resources: 1. Charts of persons suffering from the effects of eating too much. 2. Charts and poster showing substances that are harmful to the body. 3. Charts and posters showing: - a drunkard - a drug abuser.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. mention two healthy feeding practices; 2. list two effects of overeating 3. mention three uses of food additives 4. mention three substances that are harmful to the body; 5. state two effects of harmful substances to the body. 6. state the effects of drug abuse

resources.title: Farm Structures and Buildings
resources.description: Theme: PROCESSES OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Sub-theme: PROCESSES OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Content: 1. Description of farm structures and farm buildings. (a) Farm structures - barn, silos, rhombus, etc. - paddock, fish pond, etc. (b) Farm building: - poultry house, pen, store, office, utility building, security post, etc. 2. Uses of farm structures and farm buildings. 3. Maintenance of farm structures and buildings.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1 describe and identify various types of farm structures and buildings; 2. list the uses of farm structures; 3. state the method of maintaining farm structures and building.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Arrange for learners to visit commercial farm. 2. Give a board summary

Students: Use pictures and charts to identify farm structures and buildings. 2. Copy board summary
resources.resources: Pictures and charts and relevant textbooks showing farm structures.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. list farm structures. 2. state two uses of farm structures. 3. mention two methods of maintaining farm structures. 4. draw some farm structures.

resources.title: Crop Propagation and Cultural Practices
resources.description: Theme: PROCESSES OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Sub-theme: PROCESSES OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Content: 1. Meaning of Propagation. 2. Methods of Crop Propagation: - by seed (sexual) - by vegetative organs (asexual) 3. Advantages of Propagation by: (a.) Seed (easy to carry, store, procure, sow), etc. (b.) Vegetable organs: - more resistant to diseases and pests, - matures and produces early, - Withstand adverse soil and weather conditions, etc. 4. Disadvantages of Propagation by: (a) Seed: - Reduce the amount for consumption, - Seed does not germinate easily due to dormancy. (b) Vegetative organs: - Diseases of stock is manifested in offspring easily stored, - Easily store, etc.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. define crop propagation. 2. state methods of crop propagation. 3. state the advantages and disadvantages of crop propagation methods.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Displays charts and pictures on crop propagation 2. Collects and displays samples of seeds and vegetative organs of named crop plants. 3. Demonstrates some of these operations e.g. - Thinning - Supplying - Mulching etc. 4. Give a board summary. Note: An introductory treatment only required.

Students: 1. Study charts and pictures provided and list crops propagated vegetatively and by seeds. 2. Guided class demonstration of crop propagation: - by seed. - by vegetative organs. 3. Supervised practical on cultural practices. 4. Copy board summary
resources.resources: 1. Pictures and charts of crops propagated by: Seeds and vegetative organs. 2. Crop propagation specimens (seeds, vegetative organs), soil, tins/pots, water, hand trowel, etc. 3. Simple farm tools: - Hoe, - Cutlass, - Rake, - Hand trowel etc. 4. School farm.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. briefly explain crop propagation. 2. identify two methods of crop propagation. 3. state two advantages of propagation by seed and vegetative organs. 4. list three examples of crops propagated by: - seed, - vegetative, organs.

resources.title: Agricultural Practices
resources.description: Theme: PROCESSES OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Sub-theme: PROCESSES OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Content: 1. Pre-planting operations: - Choice of site, - Clearing, - Stumping, - Plotting, - Tilling/ ploughing, harrowing, ridging, - Seed selection - Nursery and nursery practices. 2. Planting operations: - Seed treatment , - Spacing and planting. 3. Post planting operations: - Thinning, - Supplying, - mulching, - Manuring/fertilizer application, - Harvesting. 4. Effects of timely harvesting versus late harvesting. 5. Post-harvest operation: - processing of crop into useable forms, - storage, etc.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. describe: - pre-planting, - planting, - post planting, - harvesting and - post harvesting operations; 2. perform the various cultural practices above; 3. explain the benefits of timely harvesting of crops.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Displays charts and pictures board. 2. Guides students to identify and describe different pre- planting operations. 3. Demonstrates some of these operations. 4. Give a board summary.

Students: 1. Study charts and pictures provided and identify the various operations depicted. 2. Watch teacher demonstrations. 3. Perform the various planting operations. 4. Copy board summary
resources.resources: . Simple farm tools: - Hoe, - Cutlass, - Rake, - Hand trowel etc. 4. School farm
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. describe briefly activities involved in: - pre-planting, - planting, - post planting, - harvesting, - post harvesting operations; 2. demonstrate the various operations; 3. state three advantages of timely harvesting of crops.

resources.title: Animal Feeds and Feeding
resources.description: Theme: PROCESSES OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Sub-theme: PROCESSES OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Content: 1. Meaning of Feed 2. Types of Feed: - energy- yielding feeds. - protein -yielding feeds. 3. Feeding Tools: - troughs, - drinker set, etc
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. state the meaning of feed. 2. list types of feed stuffs. 3. mention feeding tools.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Exhibit samples of feedstuffs such as groundnut cake, palm kernel cake, cotton seed cake, forage, silage, hay, etc. 2. Display feeding tools 3. Give a board summary.

Students: 1. Identify the various feeding tools. 2. Identify the nutrients got from the various samples of feedstuffs. 3. Use the feedstuffs to feed farm animals.
resources.resources: 1. Samples of feeds e.g. groundnut cakes, hay, including poultry feeds, etc. 2. Feeding tools: silage, feeding trough, etc.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. state what animal feed stand for. 2. list 3 types of feedstuffs. 3. name two feeding tools.

resources.title: Animal Pests and Disease Control
resources.description: Theme: PROCESSES OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Sub-theme: PROCESSES OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Content: 1. Farm animal diseases: a) Bacteria: - mastitis - contagious abortion in ruminants, pigs, etc. b) Fungal: - ring worm (all farm animals) c) Viral: - foot and mouth disease (all animals except poultry) d) Protozoan: - coccidiosis in poultry and rabbit - trypanosomiasis (nagana) (cattle) e) Worms (all farm animals) f) Nutritional-bloat (cattle)
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. list farm animal diseases; 2. state modes of transmission of farm animal diseases; 3. identify symptoms of farm animals. diseases.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Displays pictures and charts of – disease organisms like worms. - dead animals. 2. Develops chart on causal organisms, symptoms and animals affected.

Students: 1. Visit abattoir to observe meat inspection. 2. Guided discussion on animal disease causing organisms and disease symptoms. 3. Carry out good sanitation practices on the school farm animals.
resources.resources: 1. Pictures and charts of diseases of farm animals, disease organisms. 2. Preserved specimens of diseases causing organisms.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. list five farm animal diseases. 2. mention four organisms that cause farm animal diseases. 3. state four modes of transmission of farm animal diseases.

resources.title: Fishery
resources.description: Theme: PROCESSES OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Sub-theme: PROCESSES OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Content: 1. Definition of fishery. 2. Classes of fish based on: a. Habitat: - fresh water fish and salt water fish. b. Morphology e.g. Bony and cartilaginous fish. c. Other types of aquatic organisms: shell fish – crab, prawn, reptile – turtle, crocodile mammals – hippopotamus, whale. 3. Uses of fish and fish products 4. Methods of fishing. 5. Risk factors in water and fish farming: - polluting water with chemicals/industrial effluents - contaminating fish with chemicals used for catching fish.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. define fishery 2. classify fishes on the basis of habitat and morphology. 3. state the uses of fish and fish products. 4. identify methods of fishing. 5. state risk factors associated with fish farming.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Arrange a visit to a near-by fish farm. 2. Present pictures and charts on fish and fish products. 3. Display fish and the fish products. 4. Practice how to mend fishing net. 5. Discuss the effects of chemicals on fish and their environment. 5. Give a board summary.

Students: 1. Examine and identify various types of fish and other aquatic organisms displayed. 2. Identify various fishing equipment displayed. 3. Bring samples of fish and fish products. 4.Explain suitable environment for fish farming. 5. Copy board summary.
resources.resources: 1. Pictures and charts on fish and fish products. 2. Fishing nets, basket, fishing hook etc. 3. Visit to a near-by fishery.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. define fishery 2. classify fishes based on a) habitat and b) morphology. 3. state two uses of fish and fish products. 4. write three methods of fishing. 5. state how water and fish can be contaminated.

resources.title: Forests and Forest Uses
resources.description: Theme: PROCESSES OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Sub-theme: PROCESSES OF AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION | Content: 1. Types of Forests: - Mangrove (swampy), - Rain forest (many trees), - Derive forest (few trees), 2. Forest Resources: - Trees - Wildlife (animals), - Fruits (Foodstuffs), - Various Herbs, - Shelter, 3. Uses of forest resources, 4. Effect of forest on the environment. 5. Human activities that affect the forest: - clearing/deforestation, - hunting, bush burning farming,/depletion of wild life, etc.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. describe forests. 2. list the resources of the forest. 3. state the uses of the forest resources. 4. explain the effect of forest on the environment. 5. state the various human activities that affect the forest.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Facilitate guided discussion on: - resource - potentials of the forest. - forest products e.g. fruits, gums, animals, etc. 2. Visit to the saw mill or carpenter. 3. Give a board summary

Students: 1. State resources obtained from the forest and discuss their uses. 2. Copy board summary.
resources.resources: 1. Pictures and charts showing forest products. 2. Real product where available.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. describe a forest. 2. list 4 resources found in the forest. 3. state five uses of the forest. 4. describe three effects of the forest on the environment. 5. list 3 human activities which result in loss of forest resources.

resources.title: Resources and Decision Making
resources.description: Theme: FAMILY LIVING AND RESOURCE MANAGEMENT | Sub-theme: FAMILY LIVING AND RESOURCE MANAGEMENT | Content: 1. Meaning and types of family resource; 2. Meaning and steps in decision making; 3. Simple personal and family decisions.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of family resources; 2. enumerate faimly resources 3. explain the meaning of decision making; 4. enumerate the steps in decision making; 5. state simple personal and family decisions
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the meaning , type and importance of family resources, and decision making. 2. Facilitates class discussion; 3. Guides students in making personal decisions. 4. Gives a borad summary

Students: 1. Participate in discussions. 2. Make personal decision based on the steps learnt. 3. Copy the board summary.
resources.resources: 1. Charts of family resources 2. Chart indicating steps in decision making.
resources.assessment: Students should: 1. explain the meaning of family resources 2. list four family resources; 3. explain each step in decision making; 4. state two simple personal decisions 5. state any five family decisions.

resources.title: Care of Family Clothing and Household Linen
resources.description: Theme: CLOTHING AND TEXTILE | Sub-theme: CLOTHING AND TEXTILE | Content: 1. Types of household; 2. Factors that enhance the selection of household linen 3. Clothing repairs; 4. Maintenance of household linen. 5. Clothing storage.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain methods of storing family clothing; 2. carry out simple clothing repairs 3. list the types of household linen; 4. state the factors that enhance selection of household linen; 5. enumerate the procedures for maintaining household linen.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Facilitates discussion on methods of storage. 2. Demonstrates steps in clothing repairs. 3. Guides students’ to discuss the different types of household linen. 4. Explains maintenance of household linen. 5. Gives a board summary

Students: 1. Participate in class discussion. 2. Carry out simple clothing repairs. 3. Demonstrate clothing storage 4. Demonstrate maintenance of household linen 5. Copy the summary.
resources.resources: 1. Sewing kits 2. Charts and albums of household linen. 3. Magazines on different clothing items. 4. Items for clothing storage and maintenance.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. list three methods of storing family clothing; 2. fix loose buttons and mend a torn garment 3. list three types of household linen; 4. state three factors that can enhance the selection of household linen; 5. identify two methods for maintaining household linen.

resources.title: Basic Pattern Drafting Techniques and Fashion Designing
resources.description: Theme: CLOTHING AND TEXTILE | Sub-theme: CLOTHING AND TEXTILE | Content: 1. Meaning of pattern drafting and fashion designing. 2. Basic pattern drafting tools and equipment. 3. Using instructions to sketch the styles. 4. Taking body measurements 5. Drafting basic bodice and skirt patterns.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of pattern drafting and fashion designing. 2. list tools and equipment for pattern drafting; 3. identify the parts of the body to be measured; 4. take relevant basic measurements 5. draft basic bodice and skirt pattern.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Facilitates discussion on - tools and equipment for taking body measurements and parts of the body to be measured. 2. Demonstrates body measurement and pattern drafting. 3. Guides students as they work. 4. Gives a board summary.

Students: 1. Take part in the discussion. 2. Sketch styles 3. Take body measurements 4. Copy instructions for drafting the bodice and skirt patterns 5. Draft basic bodice and skirt patterns. 6. Adapt the basic block into different styles.
resources.resources: 1. Tape measure long ruler, pencil, arm hole and skirt guides, T square, brown paper; French curve, plus dressmakers carbon, tracing wheel. 2. Charts on tools and procedures for pattern drafting. 3. Drafted pattern pieces. 4. Finished articles and display
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. list two tools and two equipment for pattern drafting; 2. identify four parts of the body to be measured; 3. draft a basic bodice and skirt pattern for self.

resources.title: Food Purchasing, Processing, Preservation and Safety
resources.description: Theme: FOOD AND NUTRITION | Sub-theme: FOOD AND NUTRITION | Content: 1. Meaning of food purchasing, processing and preservation; 2. Perishable and non- perishable foods. 3. Risk factors in purchasing 4. Factors to consider when buying food. 5. Wise buying practices; 6. Reasons for food preservation. 7. Preservation methods, e.g. freezing, sun- drying salting, etc. 8. Food processing methods e.g. milling, fermentation. Etc. 9. How to keep food safe.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of food purchasing, processing,preserv ation and safety; 2. identify risks factors to consider when buying food; 3. identify factors to consider when buying food; 4. mention wise buying practices; 5. mention some food processing methods; 6. different storage/ preservation and storage methods and reasons. 7. explain how to keep food safe.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Discusses the meaning of food purchasing, processing, preservation/storage and safety; 2. Explains tips to reduce risk factors when buying food; 3. Discusses wise buying and factors to consider when buying food; 4. Discusses food porocessingmethods and effects of inappropriate prcessing of food; 5. Discusses preservation for perishable and non- perishable foods; 6. Demonstrates food preservation/ storage. 7. Explains how to ensure safety of foods e.g. food labeling. 8. Gives a board summary.

Students: 1. Participate in discussion. 2. Demonstrate food preservation/sto rage methods 3. Participate in the labeling of food containers. 4. Copy the board summary.
resources.resources: 1. Charts on perishable and non-perishable foods 2. Tools and equipment and materials for preservation 3. Perishable e.g. fruits, vegetable; 4. Food items e.g. vegetables, fruits, yams, plantains, cereals for processing/ preservation and storage. 5. Samples of preserved foods
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. list four wise buying practices; 2. mention four factors to consider when buying food; 3. list three reasons for preservation of food 4. explain methods for processing and preserving food items. 5. demonstrate food processing, preservation/ storage. 6. state three risk factors in food handling

resources.title: Packaging Criteria
resources.description: Theme: PRODUCE PACKAGING AND MARKETING | Sub-theme: PRODUCE PACKAGING AND MARKETING | Content: 1. Packaging Criteria: - Nature of the produce ( liquid or solid and shape) - Bulkiness (size) - Live or frozen or dry stock - Distance to market 2. Example of Packaging Items: - Boxes - Drum/Barrels - Cages - Polythene - Trays etc
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. identify what influences the choice of materials to use in packaging farm produce for sale 2. give examples of some types of packaging materials in agriculture
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides class discussion of the variety of packaging materials in use in agriculture. 2. Guides discussion on what influences choice of materials for packaging farm produce. 3. Give a board summary

Students: 1. Partake in providing information on packaging items they have seen before. 2. Copy board summary
resources.resources: Samples of locally available packaging items, e.g. egg trays, perforated boxes, palm- frond cages etc
resources.assessment: Students to : 1. state why some packaging items cannot be used for all farm produce 2. list 4 examples of local packaging items

resources.title: Pricing and Advertising
resources.description: Theme: PRODUCE PACKAGING AND MARKETING | Sub-theme: PRODUCE PACKAGING AND MARKETING | Content: 1. Definition of Pricing 2. Price Determinants: - cost of production - quality of produce - quantity of produce - forces of demand and supply - market price - seasonal produce
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. define pricing 2. mention factors which determine the price of agricultural produce
resources.activities:
Teacher: Facilitate class discussion on composition of produce prices

Students: Describe what the price is composed of
resources.resources: Charts of sellers and buyers in the market place
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. explain what pricing is all about 2. list 5 factors which influence the price of farm produce

resources.title: Records and Book Keeping
resources.description: Theme: PRODUCE PACKAGING AND MARKETING | Sub-theme: PRODUCE PACKAGING AND MARKETING | Content: 1 1.Definition of Farm records. 2. Use of farm records: - to monitor the progress of the business. 3. Types and uses of farm records: - farm diary, - farm inventory, - Input records, - Production records, - consumption records, - sales records, - profit and loss account. 4. Computer Aided Farm records and its benefit. 5. Definition of Book keeping: - keeping account of financial activity of enterprise. 6. Source documents: - Sales invoice, - Purchase invoice, - Returns inwards, - Returns outwards. 7. Journal preparation: - Sales journal -Purchase journal etc.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain what farm records are; 2. state the importance of farm records in agriculture; 3. list and explain the types of farm records; 4. describe the computer aided farm records and its benefits; 5. state what book keeping mean; 6. identify source documents; 7. prepare journal from source document.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Displays different types of farm records. 2. Invites a farm manager to explain more on the uses of farm records. 3. Develop charts of journals. 4. Facilitate discussion on how to prepare journals. 5. Give a board summary.

Students: 1. Partake in discussion on computer aided record and its benefits. 2. Study charts of journal and practice preparation of journal as a form of book keeping. 3. Copy board summary.
resources.resources: 1. Specimens of farm records. 2. Charts and pictures of various types of journals.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. define farm records; 2. write short essay on computer aided farm records and its benefits; 3. match the farm record with the uses; 4. state the meaning of book keeping in agriculture. 5. state 3 source document; 6. prepare journal using sales and purchase invoice documents.

resources.title: Agriculture in Stock Exchange
resources.description: Theme: PRODUCE PACKAGING AND MARKETING | Sub-theme: PRODUCE PACKAGING AND MARKETING | Content: 1. Meaning of stock: buying and selling of goods and services available now and in the future. 2. People involved in stock exchange: - buyers, - sellers, - buyers and sellers - farmers’ agents 3. Importance of stock exchange in agriculture: - encourages investment in agriculture. - encourages contract farming.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain what stock exchange is. 2. list those involved in stock exchange. 3. state the importance of stock exchange to agriculture.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides classroom discussion on stock exchange in agriculture. 2. Invites guest speaker from Agricultural Stock Exchange. 3. Give a board summary

Students: 1. Guided discussion on agriculture in stock exchange 2. Copy board summary
resources.resources: Posters and charts of agricultural stock exchange offers.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. explain stock exchange practice in agriculture. 2. mention people involved in stock exchange. 3. mention 2 benefits of stock exchange in agriculture.

resources.title: Export Promotion in Agriculture
resources.description: Theme: PRODUCE PACKAGING AND MARKETING | Sub-theme: PRODUCE PACKAGING AND MARKETING | Content: 1. Meaning of export promotion: - Encouraging sale of Nigerian produce in other countries. 2. Examples of Nigerian export produce: - Cocoa - Palm Produce - Hides & Skins - Cassava crop - Groundnut - Pepper etc. 3. Benefits of export promotion: - Attracts foreign money (exchange), - Serves as additional market outlet to farmers to earn income etc.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain what export promotion is. 2. identify Nigerian export produce. 3. state the importance of export promotion.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides classroom discussion on export promotion in agriculture. 2. Shows samples of export produce. 3. Give a board summary

Students: 1. Participate in class discussion on export produce. 2. Copy board summary.
resources.resources: Posters and charts on export promotion.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. explain the meaning of export promotion. 2. list 5 Nigerian export produce. 3. mention 2 benefits of export promotion to agriculture.

resources.title: Consumer Challenges and Rights
resources.description: Theme: FAMILY LIVING AND RESOURCE MANAGEMENT | Sub-theme: FAMILY LIVING AND RESOURCE MANAGEMENT | Content: 1. Definition of consumer 2. Rights of the consumer. 3. Challenges of the consumer. 4. Redress options for consumers. 5. Procedure for seeking redress.
resources.objectives: students should be able to: 1. define consumer; 2. State the rights of consumers; 3. discuss the challenges of consumers; 4. state the different types of redress for the consumer; 5. discuss procedures for seeking redress.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Defines a consumer 2. Explains consumer rights; 3. Guides discussions on challenges and redress options and procedures for consumers. 4. Gives a board summary

Students: 1. Participate in the discussion 2. Role-play the Rights of Consumers. 3. Go on field trip to the market to practice the identified solutions.
resources.resources: 1. Charts, 2. Fliers 3. Video clip, 4. Pictures, 5. Flash cards, 6. Posters showing market scenes and products. 7. Relevant reading materials.
resources.assessment: students to: 1. define consumer right; 2. list six universal consumer rights; 3. list five challenges faced by consumers; 4. state five ways of overcoming the challenges faced by consumers; 5. state three types of redress options available to consumers.

resources.title: Child Development and Care
resources.description: Theme: FAMILY LIVING AND RESOURCE MANAGEMENT | Sub-theme: FAMILY LIVING AND RESOURCE MANAGEMENT | Content: 1. Meaning and stages of child development. 2. Factors that influence child development. 3. Conditions necessary for child development. 4. Care of the child. 5. Common childhood ailments. 6. Immuniztaion for children.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. describe the meaning and different stages in child development 2. list factors that influence child development 3. describe the conditions necessary for child development 4. describe the different types of care required by a child 5. describe the common childhood ailments 6. enumerate the different types of immunization required by a child.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides discussion on: - stages of child development - factors necessary for child development and conditions necessary for child development; 2. Guides discussion on child care. 3. Invites a guest speaker on child development; 4. Gives a board summary.

Students: 1. Participate in discussion on stages of child development. 2. Copy the board summary.
resources.resources: 1. Charts, toys and play materials for children, films, video clips; 2. Charts showing diffrent stages of child development; 3. Charts showing children with different childhood ailments 4. Charts showing types of immunization according to age. 5. Posters on immunization.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. describe three stages of child development 2. enumerate five factors that influence child development 3. explain four conditions that are necessary for child development 4. explain three types of care required by a child 5. describe three types of immunization against child ailments.

resources.title: Textiles: types, properties, production, uses and care.
resources.description: Theme: CLOTHING AND TEXTILE | Sub-theme: CLOTHING AND TEXTILE | Content: 1. Definition of textile with examples 2. Basic textile terms e.g. fiber; yarn, warp, weft 3. Reasons for studying textiles 4. Importance of textiles 5. Differences between natural and synthetic fibers 6. Properties, care and uses of fibers 7. Production of textiles e.g. woven table mat. 8. Laundering of fabrics
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. define textiles with examples 2. explain basic textile terms. 3. state reasons for studying textiles 4. discuss the uses or importance of textiles to man. 5. list different classes of textiles 6. differentiate between natural and synthetic fibers 7. state properties of each type textile 8. produce woven table mats. 9. Launder a fabric.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the term textiles 2. Discusses reasons for studying textiles 3. Demonstrates the making of fabrics using strips of cardboard sheets 4. Shows ways of taking care of fibers 5. Discusses the uses of both natural and synthetic fibers. 6. Demonstrates production of woven table mat. 7. Demonstrates laundry work. 8. Gives a board summary.

Students: 1. Participate in the discussions 2. Practice weaving skill using strips of paper to produce woven mats. 3. Practice laundry work; 4. Copy the board summary
resources.resources: 1. Cotton wool, sewing yarn, pieces of fabrics, cardboard sheets, pencil, scissors, etc. 2. Basin, water, detergent or soap bars, laundry brush, washing accessories, cold water starch, dyeing agent.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. explain four textile terms 2. give four reasons for studying textiles 3. list four uses of textile 4. list three properties, each of both natural and synthetic fibers. 5. identify three ways of taking care of different textiles 6. state two ways of producing textiles; 7. produce woven table cloth.

resources.title: Sewing Machine and Garment Construction Processes
resources.description: Theme: CLOTHING AND TEXTILE | Sub-theme: CLOTHING AND TEXTILE | Content: 1. Types and parts of the sewing machine 2. Factors that influence choice of a sewing machine 3. Care of sewing machine 4. Terms peculiar to garment construction e.g. facing, hems, openings, fastenings, etc. 5. Making of a simple baby dress using the sewing machine.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. identify different types of sewing machines 2. identify the parts of the sewing machine and state their functions 3. explain the guidelines for chosing sewing machines 4. explain the process of taking care of the sewing machines 5. explain the meaning of some terms used in garment construction. 6. Use the sewing machine to produce baby dress.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Discusses types, parts and functions of each part of the sewing machine. 2. Discusses the factors to consider when choosing sewing machines 3. Guides students in discussing the meaning and making of darts, tucks, openings, facings. Fastenings, hems, etc 4. Demonstrates the making of a simple baby dress; 5. Gives a board summary

Students: 1. Take part in the discussion 2. Examine the parts of the sewing machine 3. Operate a sewing machine 4. Make specimen of facing, hems, openings and fastening 5. Make a simple baby’s dress. 6. Copy the board summary
resources.resources: 1. Charts, 2. Real objects e.g. sewing machines 3. Specimen of facing hems, openings and fastenings 4. Charts showing construction processes 5. Sewing tools, equipment and materials.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. list three types of sewing machine; 2. explain five parts of a sewing machine and state their functions; 3. explain factors to consider when choosing a sewing machine; 4. make two straight and curved stitches on a piece of fabric using a sewing machine; 5. explain four ways of taking care of a sewing machine 6. make a simple baby dress.

resources.title: Food Hygiene and Safety

resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Discusses the: - meaning of food hygiene - reasons for healthy food handling - food poisoning and - food safety 2. Demonstrates methods of handling left-over foods. 3. Demonstrates how to cover their lunch. 4. Discuss sensory signs of spoilage and causative micro-organisms 5. Gives a board summary

Students: 1. Participate in the discussion 2. Practice how to cover their lunch packs properly 3. Mention ways of handling food in their homes. 4. Copy the board summary.
resources.resources: 1. Raw foods on display 2. Chart showing stored foods 3. Food warmers (picnic boxes), plastic packs, cellophane or polythene bags, utensils and plates.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. give two reasons for covering food; 2. state two ways of handling food for safety; 3. state the meaning of food hygiene; 4. explain the meaning of food poisoning; 5. state two effects of consuming contaminated food; 6. describe three sensory signs of spoilage and causative micro- organisms; 7. list two causative micro-organisms.

resources.title: Preparation, Packaging and Marketing of Food Items
resources.description: Theme: FOOD AND NUTRITION | Sub-theme: FOOD AND NUTRITION | Content: 1. Differences between snacks and main meals. 2. Snacks and drinks available in the society. 3. Duties of food sellers/provide rs for the public. 4. Preparation of snacks, drinks and meals. 5. Preparation of food for packaging. 6. Marketing principles.
resources.objectives: The students should be able to: 1. state the differences between snacks and main menu; 2. mention snacks and drinks that could be prepared, packaged and marketed easily; 3. list the duties of food providers for public consumption; 4. prepare and serve simple snacks, drinks and meals.

Teacher: 1. Guides students discussion of: - the responsibilities of food safety managers; and - the effect of unhygienic food handling to the consumers; 2. Gives a board summary

resources.resources: 3. Samples of food items. 4. Charts of food safety regulations.
